Possession after possession has been wrested from her in Europe, Asia, and Africa. arxiv-2207-05905.title: Buoyancy segregation suppresses viscous fingering in horizontal displacements in a porous layer
arxiv-2207-05905.creator: Edward M. Hinton 1 and Apoorv Jyoti 2
arxiv-2207-05905.description: Abstract We consider the axisymmetric displacement of an ambient fluid by a second input fluid of lower density and lower viscosity in a horizontal porous layer. If the two fluids have been vertically segregated by buoyancy, the flow becomes self-similar with the input fluid preferentially flowing near the upper boundary.

arxiv-2209-01972.title: On the chaotic expansion for counting processes This research is supported by a grant of the French National Research Agency (ANR), “Investissements d’Avenir” (LabEx Ecodec/ANR-11-LABX-0047) and the Joint Research Initiative "Cyber Risk Insurance: actuarial modeling" with the partnership of AXA Rese
arxiv-2209-01972.creator: Caroline Hillairet, Anthony Réveillac
arxiv-2209-01972.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Caroline Hillairet, Anthony Réveillac. We introduce and study an alternative form of the chaotic expansion for counting processes using the Poisson imbedding representation; we name this alternative form pseudo-chaotic expansion . As an application, we prove that the coefficients of this pseudo-chaotic expansion for any linear Hawkes process are obtained in closed form, whereas those of the usual chaotic expansion cannot be derived explicitly.

arxiv-2304-11094.title: Effectiveness of Debiasing Techniques: An Indigenous Qualitative Analysis
arxiv-2304-11094.creator: Vithya Yogarajan & Gillian Dobbie, Henry Gouk
arxiv-2304-11094.description: Abstract An indigenous perspective on the effectiveness of debiasing techniques for pre-trained language models (PLMs) is presented in this paper. The current techniques used to measure and debias PLMs are skewed towards the US racial biases and rely on pre-defined bias attributes (e.g. “black” vs “white”). Some require large datasets and further pre-training.

arxiv-2403-11375.title: Path-GPTOmic: A Balanced Multi-modal Learning Framework for Survival Outcome Prediction
arxiv-2403-11375.creator: Hongxiao Wang Yang Yang Zhuo Zhao Pengfei Gu Nishchal Sapkota Danny Z. Chen
arxiv-2403-11375.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hongxiao Wang Yang Yang Zhuo Zhao Pengfei Gu Nishchal Sapkota Danny Z. Chen. For predicting cancer survival outcomes, standard approaches in clinical research are often based on two main modalities: pathology images for observing cell morphology features, and genomic (e.g., bulk RNA-seq) for quantifying gene expressions. However, existing pathology-genomic multi-modal algorithms face significant challenges: (1) Valuable biological insights regarding genes and gene-gene interactions are frequently overlooked; (2) one modality often dominates the optimization process, causing inadequate training for the other modality.

arxiv-2404-09508.title: From laminar to chaotic flow via stochastic resonance in viscoelastic channel flow
arxiv-2404-09508.creator: Yuke Li, Victor Steinberg
arxiv-2404-09508.description: Abstract Recent research indicates that low-inertia viscoelastic channel flow experiences supercritical non-normal mode elastic instability from laminar to sustained chaotic flow due to finite-size perturbations. The challenge of this study is to elucidate a realization of such a pathway when the intensity of the elastic wave is too low to amplify velocity fluctuations above the instability onset.

arxiv-2407-11915.title: Imitation of human motion achieves natural head movements for humanoid robots in an active-speaker detection task
arxiv-2407-11915.creator: Bosong Ding, Murat Kirtay, Giacomo Spigler
arxiv-2407-11915.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bosong Ding, Murat Kirtay, Giacomo Spigler. Head movements are crucial for social human-human interaction. They can transmit important cues (e.g., joint attention, speaker detection) that cannot be achieved with verbal interaction alone. This advantage also holds for human-robot interaction. Even though modeling human motions through generative AI models has become an active research area within robotics in recent years, the use of these methods for producing head movements in human-robot interaction remains underexplored.

arxiv-2506-19511.title: Integrating Pair Programming as a Work Practice
arxiv-2506-19511.creator: Nina Haugland Andersen, Anastasiia Tkalich, Nils Brede Moe, Darja Šmite, Asgaut Mjølne Söderbom, Ola Hast, Viktoria Stray
arxiv-2506-19511.description: Abstract Context: Pair programming (PP) is more relevant than ever. As modern systems grow in complexity, knowledge sharing and collaboration across teams have become essential. However, despite well-documented benefits of PP, its adoption remains inconsistent across software teams. Objective: This study aims to understand the factors that facilitate or hinder team members’ adoption as well as lasting engagement in PP.

arxiv-2512-14414.title: A single-layer framework of variational tensor network states
arxiv-2512-14414.creator: Hongyu Chen, Yangfeng Fu, Weiqiang Yu, Rong Yu, Z. Y. Xie
arxiv-2512-14414.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hongyu Chen, Yangfeng Fu, Weiqiang Yu, Rong Yu, Z. Y. Xie. We propose a single-layer tensor network framework for the variational determination of ground states in two-dimensional quantum lattice models. By combining the nested tensor network method [Phys. B 96 , 045128 (2017)] with the automatic differentiation technique, our approach can reduce the computational cost by three orders of magnitude in bond dimension, and therefore enables highly efficient variational ground-state calculations.

pmc-11652918.creator: Mahmud Ahmednur, Remla Sabir, Dechassa Lenjissa, Argaw Ambelu
pmc-11652918.description: Freshwater ecosystems are increasingly modified worldwide by anthropogenic activities. Land use change is one of the leading factors responsible for stream ecosystem degradation. Physical habitat disturbance due to channelization is among the factors responsible for the loss of biodiversity and degradation of river water quality worldwide.

pmc-12386429.title: The Supportive Role of Plant-Based Substances in AMD Treatment and Their Potential
pmc-12386429.creator: Karolina Klusek, Magdalena Kijowska, Maria Kiełbus, Julia Sławińska, Dominika Kuźmiuk, Tomasz Chorągiewicz, Robert Rejdak, Joanna Dolar-Szczasny, Ana Paula Coelho Duarte
pmc-12386429.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). There is growing interest in the use of natural plant-derived compounds, such as polyphenols (including curcumin), flavonoids, silymarin, anthocyanins, lutein, and zeaxanthin, for the treatment of age-related macular degeneration (AMD). These substances exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and protective effects on retinal cells, contributing to the preservation of retinal integrity by modulating the key pathogenic mechanisms of AMD, including oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and pathological neovascularization. Consequently, they hold potential to support conventional therapeutic approaches and slow disease progression.

The expression levels of DUSP2 in the peripheral blood of AKI and non‐AKI patients were first examined.

pmc-13402168.creator: Xuexing Luo, Zhichao Pei, Amy Jing-Wen Yin
pmc-13402168.description: While generative artificial intelligence enables large-scale, individualized, and digitally scalable interventions, its deployment introduces model instability and algorithmic reasoning errors. To ensure patient safety, the next frontier for AI-assisted music medicine therapeutics is not merely tool optimization, but the implementation of a transparent, rule-based clinical safety guardrail.
